The app is collecting the articles in your topics and preparing them for instant random reading. The first topic is usually ready in under a minute; you can start browsing as soon as it is, and the rest keeps building in the background.
The rest of your topics will keep building in the background. You can start browsing now; each remaining topic becomes available as soon as it is ready.

Wikitext is the fast native renderer. HTML uses Wikipedia\'s rendered page with its links and inline formatting, but needs a fresh network request for every article.

The reading history stored in Firebase will be deleted. History on this device stays, and automatic sync is turned off. Your sign-in account and email are not deleted here. Other devices that still sync may upload their local history again, so turn sync off there too. You can turn sync back on here later.

Quietly prepare the next random articles (text and pictures) while you read, so they open instantly. Uses a little extra data.

Swipe to go back and forward
Swipe right on an article to go back in history and left to go forward. Edge swipes are left free for the menu and tabs.
Use Wikivoyage travel guides instead of Wikipedia for search, topics and random articles. Turn this off again to return to Wikipedia; restart the app after changing it.
Show the introduction to WikiRandomizer-P again
A one-minute tour of what makes it fast and fun. You can replay it any time from Settings.
Choose what you are curious about (science, history, music and more) and WikiRandomizer-P builds a library of matching articles. You can also long-press the shuffle button any time to change them.
Tap the shuffle button at the bottom to open a random article from your topics. The next one is already being prepared while you read, so it opens instantly.
While reading, pull the article down to jump straight to a new random article.
Slide a finger to the right from the left side of the screen to open the menu, without reaching for the button at the top.
Slide a finger from the right edge of the screen to open your tabs. Hold a link for a second to add its article to your tabs without leaving the page you are reading.
Tap the thumbs up or thumbs down at the bottom to get more or fewer articles like the one you are reading.
Save articles for later, search with the bar at the top, switch the article language or share a page. Articles you have already opened load instantly, even offline.
Everything lives in Settings: themes, colours, text size, language, reading history and the topic library. Open it now and take a look; the tour carries on when you come back.
Enjoy exploring! You can replay this tour from Settings at any time.

WikiRandomizer-P is free, has no ads and collects no data. If it makes your day a little better, you can support its development. This is completely optional.
